workflow.critical: Execute through {project-root}/_arcwright/core/tasks/workflow.xml with {installed_path}/workflow.yaml loaded. Honor user/host scope, permissions, languages, and interaction mode; reuse the shared runtime and applicable AGENTS.md.
Creating a story prepares an implementation plan. It does not authorize implementation, subsequent stories, or a whole epic. Preserve any explicit wider authorization already given.

step.action: Resolve the supplied story_path, epic/story identifier, or task brief. For an explicitly requested next story, inspect sprint_status in order and select the first backlog story. Do not require sprint tracking when a target is already provided.

Set epic_num, story_num, story_key, story_id, and story_title from verified context. If the target is still consequentially ambiguous or no requested backlog story exists, ask for the missing target rather than silently choosing another scope.
Read the target epic/story requirements, using its shard or relevant headings. Identify acceptance criteria, scope boundaries, dependencies, and any existing story file/customizations before writing.

step.goal: Gather the context needed for this story
step.action: Use the story/epic context and verifiable unchanged research first. Use discover_inputs only for missing context; load indexes/relevant sections and expand for specific gaps. Do not preload entire document collections.

Cover the following dimensions where relevant, directly or through authorized specialist work: - Requirements: acceptance criteria, constraints, and dependency stories from the epic/PRD. - Architecture: existing paths, APIs, models/migrations, auth/ownership rules, failure/performance constraints, and reusable patterns. - UX: affected screens/flows, design system, accessibility, responsive behavior, loading/error/empty states. - Prior work: relevant previous-story decisions, established utilities/tests, and targeted path history when it resolves uncertainty. - Project standards: applicable AGENTS.md and existing code/fixtures. Read host-specific imports only when applicable to the active host.
Determine is_ui_story from the requested behavior. Missing UX docs are a context gap, not evidence that the story is backend-only.

Select useful skills from catalog metadata or the arcwright router; load only chosen entrypoints and needed references. Load test-quality before recommending new tests. Do not add a compression skill merely to write a concise plan.

check.if: substantial independent research or review is authorized and useful
check.action: Use installed subagent-protocol, bounded concurrency, distinct ownership, relevant skill paths/finder, and concise source-bound handoffs. Combine related questions in the smallest useful specialist set; no agent-per-artifact requirement applies. Do not delegate routine lookup or duplicate unchanged briefs.

step.action: For uncertain external APIs, compatibility, or security facts, verify primary documentation for the project's actual pinned versions. Research only relevant uncertainties; do not upgrade dependencies or survey every library's latest release just because it is named.

Ask consequential unresolved requirement questions before treating the plan as implementation-ready. Make ordinary implementation choices from existing conventions; do not invent user decisions or requirements.

Save a concise reusable research_context_file at _arcwright-output/parallel/research-context-{{story_key}}.md when useful. Include source paths/content identities, relevant conclusions, decisions, and remaining gaps; cite documents/code/URLs rather than agent/model names. Avoid raw report duplication. Follow host evidence storage for temporary logs.
Use {installed_path}/template.md for {default_output_file}, preserving useful existing authored content. Write the user story and numbered acceptance criteria from verified requirements.

Derive dependency-ordered Tasks/Subtasks mapped to acceptance criteria. Specify behavior and reusable implementation locations. Add validation tasks only where they cover a plausible risk; no subtask count or test-per-task quota applies.

Write only relevant Dev Notes: architecture/technical requirements, library compatibility, coding standards, prior-work intelligence, and references. State exact paths/APIs when verified; label uncertainty instead of guessing. Cite the underlying source, not a researcher identity.

For UI work, include relevant UX/UI Notes covering screens/components, existing design tokens/patterns, accessibility, responsiveness, and applicable states. Use a UX specialist only when authorized and useful for an unresolved design problem.

Set metadata story_key, is_ui_story, research_context_file when available, and skills_scanned. Leave implementation notes and File List for actual implementation. Do not add model/version fields, attribution labels, or generated-by notices; retain required legal/source credits.
Keep Status draft while material requirements or dependencies remain unresolved. Do not leave unresolved placeholders in a story marked ready-for-dev.

Apply {installed_path}/checklist.md: verify requirement-to-task traceability, architectural compatibility, existing functionality reuse, required UX, dependency/risk handling, and meaningful proportional verification.
Record only concrete gaps with evidence and impact. A clean result is valid. There is no minimum issue count, mandatory four-reviewer panel, or supplementary pass to manufacture findings.

Fix confirmed in-scope gaps using existing authorization. Do not expand agreed acceptance criteria to satisfy speculative review suggestions. Recheck changed sections and open findings; reuse unchanged source-bound evidence.

If independent validation is required, follow subagent-protocol and the selected review budget. Otherwise a direct quality pass suffices. Budget exhaustion or unavailable required review is not approval; retain draft status and state what remains.

step.goal: Save and return the requested plan

check.if: requirements and all required planning checks are satisfied
check.action: Set Status ready-for-dev. If sprint tracking exists, update only this story's entry, preserving comments/order. Mark a backlog epic in-progress only when its first story is actually being prepared; do not reopen a completed epic without authorization.

step.action: Save the story and concise references/context. Report story_key, path, status, decisions, and unresolved blockers.

check.if: the current task explicitly authorizes implementing this story as well as preparing it
check.action: Invoke {project-root}/_arcwright/awm/workflows/4-implementation/dev-story/workflow.yaml only when the story is ready. Pass story_path, is_ui_story, research_context_file, and the current scope/budget. Preparing this story never implicitly adds another to the authorized queue.

step.action: Otherwise return the prepared story without starting implementation, advancing to another story, or prompting for redundant permission.
